# My plan for this year

*Sitting at the kitchen table, thinking through the season ahead*

I've been working these 30.4 mu for decades. My body is slower now at 68, but my head is clear and I've seen enough weather and prices to know what works. With 8 people in the household — though some of the younger ones are working in town — I've got hands for the busy stretches but I can't expect full-time labor. I rely on the tractor for tillage and a custom combine at wheat harvest.

My main system is wheat-maize double cropping on the good flat ground, about 25 mu. I keep 5.4 mu in millet on the lighter patch near the edge — millet is what my wife makes porridge with, the grandchildren like it, and any surplus sells decent at the county market. Millet doesn't need much, doesn't like too much water, and it gives me some insurance if wheat or maize has a bad year.

## Winter wheat (25 mu, the returning crop from last October)

I planted in early October last year, Jimai 22 variety — same as most of my neighbors, reliable around here. I put down about 35 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu before planting as base, which gives me roughly 5 kg N, plus I added 8 kg N as urea with the base. Come jointing in late March, I topdressed another 10 kg N as urea — so around 18 kg N/mu total. Looked at the soil color and the crop stand, that's about right for a 480-500 kg/mu target.

I'll irrigate once more at grain filling in May if it stays dry. Already did the winter irrigation in December and the jointing irrigation. Sprayed once for aphids and powdery mildew in April — the extension station sent a warning. Harvest around June 8-12 with the hired combine, 40 yuan/mu.

## Summer maize (25 mu, right behind the wheat)

No time to waste after wheat comes off — I'll no-till plant maize within 3-5 days using my own two-row planter behind the tractor. Zhengdan 958, same variety three years running, it handles our heat. Seed costs about 15 yuan/mu.

For fertilizer I do one base at planting — 30 kg of compound plus 10 kg urea per mu, so about 10 kg N base. Then at big trumpet stage in late July I side-dress 15 kg urea per mu, another 7 kg N. Total around 17 kg N/mu. That's been my rate for years and I get 520-550 kg/mu in a normal year.

Irrigation: usually one round after planting to get a stand, and one more at silking if July is dry. Pumping costs me about 15 yuan/mu per time from the well. Spray once for armyworm and corn borer if I see them — last year they came in, this year we'll see.

## Millet (5.4 mu)

I'll plant after the wheat harvest in mid-June, Zhangzagu varieties that do well on our lighter ground. Lower input — maybe 15 kg compound fertilizer per mu at planting and that's it. Almost no irrigation needed, millet is tough. Hand-weed twice with my wife and daughter-in-law — no herbicide, this is what we eat. Harvest late September with sickles, thresh on the drying floor. I expect maybe 250-300 kg/mu.

## What I'm watching this year

Fertilizer prices jumped again, so I'm not going to push my rates higher even though on paper I could. Diesel is steady. If the spring stays dry like it feels so far, I'll have to irrigate wheat one extra time, which adds maybe 400 yuan across the wheat fields. I've got about 8,000 yuan set aside for inputs — should be enough if I'm careful. The grandchildren's school fees come in August, so I need to keep some cash back from the wheat sale.
